title: Bridge Threads sync: Cross-func roadmap prep (Julian)
content:
Context:
Quick notes to prepare for the cross-functional roadmap sync with Product (Maya), Eng (Ravi), and Applied ML (Daria). This is a working scratchpad: rough ideas, open questions and proposed sequencing for the next 6–12 weeks.
content_2:
Meeting goals:
- Align on priorities for the Bridge Threads initiative: low-latency routing, model variant rollouts, and evaluation metrics to guard quality regressions.
- Agree on canary strategy and what success looks like for a staged rollout.
- Assign owners and deadlines for the small experiments we want before the full design doc.
content_3:
Quick background:
- Bridge Threads = lightweight routing layer + policy deck that can route requests by latency SLO, cost target, or quality threshold.
- Prod constraints: Dedicated pools limited in eu-west-1 for Q3; host API burst capacity will be used during holiday promo.
- Applied ML has two candidate variants: med-quantized (fast, slightly lower n-gram recall) and fp16 baseline (slower, higher QA).
content_4:
Open questions to surface:
1) What quality delta is acceptable for beta customers? (Product to propose thresholds)
2) Is automatic fallback acceptable or should we require explicit opt-in by customers?
3) What telemetry do SRE/Console need to detect regressions early (token-level diffs, sample-based evals, p99 latency by route)?
4) Capacity: if dedicated pool saturates, do we failover to hosted API automatically or route to cheaper fp16 variant?
content_5:
Tradeoffs (sketch):
- Latency-first (med-quant): - Pros: 25–40% lower p95; Cons: edge-case hallucination uptick in long-context prompt tests (see linked evals).
- Cost-first (fp16 + batching): - Pros: lower unit cost; Cons: potential p95 regressions under bursty tail.
- Conservative rollout (manual opt-in): - Pros: safer for SLAs; Cons: slower feedback and adoption.
content_6:
Proposed canary plan (short):
Week 0: small internal canary (team traffic ~5%) — validate latency + quality with A/B eval set (Daria owns).
Week 1–2: expand to trusted beta customers (Product owns outreach & opt-in).
Week 3–4: open to 100% of non-enterprise traffic with automatic fallback.
Metrics to pass: p95 latency <= baseline * 0.95, regression on eval set <= 1.5% fail rate, error rate < 0.05%.
content_7:
API/Contract notes (engineering):
- Add route-level 'preferred_variant' flag to API (backwards compatible default = null).
- Routing policy config: JSON blob in console with precedence order: (1) customer override, (2) latency SLO, (3) cost cap.
- Need migration plan for existing pinned model routes (Ravi to draft).
content_8:
Mini decision log (today):
- Use med-quant as initial canary variant — tentative (Product + ML)
- Fallback default = fp16 baseline (engineering + SRE)
- Telemetry: require sample diffs + token-level cost breakdown (obs team)
content_9:
Action items (explicit):
- Daria: finalize eval set + run full benchmark comparing med-quant vs fp16 (due 2026-06-18)
- Ravi: draft API change PR & migration notes for pinned routes (due 2026-06-19)
- Maya: prepare beta customer email + opt-in form; scope incentives (due 2026-06-21)
- Kai: cost model update for med-quant (update internal calc sheet) (due 2026-06-16)
- Julian (me): coordinate internal canary schedule and send calendar invites (due 2026-06-15)
- Obs team (cc Daria/Ravi): add required dashboards (p95, p99, eval-fail-rate, fallback counts) (due 2026-06-20)
content_10:
Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: subtle quality regressions not captured by small eval sets. Mitigation: add randomized sampling of user traffic to human-eval pool; increase eval set diversity.
- Risk: capacity blowout in eu-west. Mitigation: enforce capacity caps per-customer and reserve burst nodes; pre-warm dedicated pools for canary window.
- Risk: customer confusion about variant behavior. Mitigation: clear console labels + changelog + product comms.
content_11:
Parking lot (follow-ups):
- Longer-term: integrate model-confidence signals into routing policy.
- Legal/compliance check for private deployments using med-quant quantized builds.
- SRE-run chaos test for fallback reliability.
content_12:
Meeting logistics:
- Proposed time: 2026-06-12 10:00 PT (30–45m).
- Attendees suggested: Maya (Product), Ravi (Eng), Daria (Applied ML), Kai (Finance/cost), Kai will also join initially for cost trade discussion, me (Julian) to run the sync.
- Pre-read: this doc + linked confluence page + Daria's benchmark draft (link above).
content_13:
Notes for discussion (to bring up live):
- How strict should our canary rollback thresholds be? (hard abort vs advisory)
- Do we want a single routing policy schema for hosted + dedicated, or allow extra flags for private deployments?
- Timeline dependency: Dedicated pool capacity in eu-west needs confirmation from infra (Ravi to ping infra on capacity by 06/14).
content_14:
Quick todo (me): send calendar, tag obs/infra teams on the doc, incorporate Daria's bench results into canary pass conditions, and lock beta customer list with Maya.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to meeting agenda after I get Daria's benchmark outputs.
